subject: Data localization & deletion evidence — SOC 2 artifact request (BrightBank)
messages:
From: Matthew Cole <matthew.cole@brightbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2025-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: residency, retention, and deletion evidence for SOC 2

Hi Evelyn,

As part of BrightBank's SOC 2 scoping for our platform integration, our InfoSec team needs evidence around Redwood's data residency, retention and deletion controls. Specifically we are hoping to get the following artifacts and brief explanations: 

- Current data retention policy (how long logs, prompts, and persisted outputs are retained by default and options to change).
- Deletion runbook / proof of deletion (sample audit showing deletion events for a customer record or S3 object).
- Explanation of cross-region replication or backups that might affect residency (are EU records ever replicated to US regions?).
- How deletion requests are processed and timeline from request to irreversible deletion.
- Any SOC 2 / ISO attachments you can share that reference retention/deletion controls (can be redacted).

We'd appreciate the artifacts redacted as necessary for other customers. Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? Our audit window is the week of Nov 10; if possible we would like the evidence by Nov 6 so we can include it in the control testing packet.

Thanks,
Matt
Matthew Cole
Senior Security Engineer — BrightBank
security@brightbank.com
(415) 555-0194
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Cole <matthew.cole@brightbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-29T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency, retention, and deletion evidence for SOC 2

Hi Matt — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a package for BrightBank. High level plan and ETA: 

- What we will provide (by Nov 5):
  * Current retention policy PDF (redwood_retention_policy_v2.pdf) with callouts for API request logs, embeddings, and model outputs.
  * Deletion runbook + sample S3 deletion audit CSV (s3_deletion_audit_2025Q3.csv) covering a redacted customer sample.
  * SOC 2 Type II retention appendix (redacted) — will include control mappings (soc2_type2_retention_appendix_redacted.pdf).
  * Short write-up on cross-region replication and backups (excerpt in the Drive folder).

- Notes: deletion events are logged and we can show object-level deletion history for a redacted sample; irreversible object removal from primary and backup stores is typically within 72 hours after the deletion job completes, but archival retention (if enabled by the customer) may be governed by their config.

To make sure we provide precisely what your auditors need, can you confirm whether you require:
  1) Evidence for a sample production customer (preferred) or synthetic sample?
  2) Any specific ISO/SOC control IDs you want us to map to?

I'll loop in Rishi and Jonas to pull the artifacts; Mina please check redaction/legal constraints.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency, retention, and deletion evidence for SOC 2

Eve — quick internal coordination. Below are the pieces we can realistically pull and considerations: 

- Retention policy: use redwood_retention_policy_v2.pdf (public-facing + internal appendix). We'll include a short excerpt that lists retention windows for logs (90 days default), request/response cache (30 days by default unless customer pins), and embeddings/LLM outputs (varies; default 30 days).
- Deletion proof: we can export an S3 event audit for a redacted acct id. The pipeline deletes objects and then emits an audit event; sample CSV will include event_time, object_key_hash (redacted), actor (service/deleted_by), and job_id.
- Backups/replication: top-level statement: we do not replicate EU-region customer data into US regions unless the customer has explicitly opted into cross-region failover. Backups are encrypted and stored in region; snapshot retention for cluster backups is 30 days by default.

Need Mina to confirm: any legal reason we cannot share the redacted S3 audit for a production customer; otherwise we can use a synthetic but realistic extract (sanitised). Also recommend we generate a one-page control mapping table that references SOC 2 CC6.2/CC8.1 equivalents and ISO 27001 A.8 (or similar) — Jonas can produce that.

I'll place artifacts in the compliance Drive folder and open SEC-4781 for tracking.

- Rishi
Director, Product Security
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Cole <matthew.cole@brightbank.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@brightbank.com>, security@brightbank.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency, retention, and deletion evidence for SOC 2

Hi Matt / BrightBank security team —

Thanks for the patience. Per our plan, please find the initial evidence artifacts attached and linked below. We redacted any customer identifiers and removed stack traces: 

Attachments included:
- redwood_retention_policy_v2.pdf — outlines default retention windows and configuration knobs.
- s3_deletion_audit_2025Q3.csv — redacted sample of deletion audit events (columns: event_time, object_key_hash, actor, job_id, region).
- soc2_type2_retention_appendix_redacted.pdf — excerpt from our audited SOC 2 Type II report focusing on retention/deletion controls and auditor commentary.

Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink
Jira ticket for tracking: SEC-4781

Key clarifications: 
- Residency: customer data created and stored in an EU or US region remains in that region by default. Cross-region replication only occurs with explicit customer opt-in for failover; snapshots and backups are stored encrypted in the same region unless opt-in is enabled.
- Deletion timeline: after a deletion request is processed, object-level removals and cache invalidation typically complete within 24–72 hours; full irreversible deletion from backups (where applicable) can take up to 30 days depending on snapshot retention settings. We document the process in the deletion runbook in the Drive folder.
- Auditability: deletion events are logged; sample CSV contains a sequential set of deletion audit events you can hand to auditors. We can provide additional log exports if the auditors need specific time windows.

Next steps — please tell us: 
1) Do the attached artifacts satisfy the auditor's needs or do they want more detail (e.g., KMS key IDs, customer-specific object keys under NDA)?
2) Would you like a short walkthrough meeting with Jonas to map controls to specific SOC/ISO IDs? I can schedule for next week.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
